title: AFP eyes kinetic weapons to boost territorial defense
summary: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) is eyeing the acquisition of kinetic weapon systems to strengthen the country's territorial defense and protect its sea lanes.

blocks.text: The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) is eyeing the acquisition of kinetic weapon systems to strengthen the country's territorial defense and protect its sea lanes.

In a report by Chino Gaston on "24 Oras" on Friday, US President Donald Trump announced a $2-billion military loan for the Philippines during his visit to the country, equivalent to around P127 billion.
Of this amount, $400 million will be allocated to strengthening the military's capabilities to deter potential attacks in the West Philippine Sea.
One of the capabilities being considered involves kinetic weapons, which can strike targets at long range on land or at sea.
These weapons use the kinetic energy generated by the speed and mass of a projectile, such as missiles and bullets, to hit their targets.

"These are weapon systems which have larger range. So, there are missile systems. The missile systems will not be effective if there is no radar. Of course, you need to detect where the threat is," Major General Oliver Maquiling, director of the AFP's DAGITPA Exercise, said in a mix of English and Filipino.
AFP Chief of Staff General Antonio Nafarrete said these weapons are important in deterring foreign vessels from entering the country's sea lanes.

"We concentrate now on kinetic requirements basically for territorial defense talaga, ensuring pag may mga… kasi ito archipelagic. Pumapasok na yung mga PLA (People's Liberation Army) na mga naval vessels dito sa sea lines of communication natin. That’s international kasi, so we must have that deterrent capability," Nafarette said.

(We are now focusing on kinetic requirements, primarily for territorial defense. Given that the Philippines is an archipelagic country and Chinese naval vessels are entering our sea lines of communication, we must have that deterrent capability.)
The deployment and use of missile systems are among the capabilities being tested and practiced during the AFP's AJEX DAGITPA military exercises.
The Philippines already operates several missile systems, including the BrahMos cruise missiles acquired from India, which have a reported range of up to 300 kilometers.
The country also has C-Star anti-ship cruise missiles from South Korea. —Jean Mangaluz/VBL, GMA News
